label: official-format-reference

sources.what: C1 Advanced exam format page: Writing 1 h 30 min, 2 parts, 220-260 words each; Part 1 compulsory essay based on an input text, explain which of two points is more important with reasons; Part 2 one task from three (letter/email, proposal, report, review); Speaking 15 min per pair (23 min for three) and the part timings.

Cambridge teacher's notes 'C1 Advanced Writing Part 1': the input gives three bullet points and three short opinions; the candidate discusses two of the points, decides which is more important or effective and gives reasons; the opinions may be used but in the candidate's own words.

Cambridge lesson 'C1 Advanced Overview of the Writing Paper': Part 1 is one compulsory task, Part 2 offers a choice of three, both parts carry equal marks, 220-260 words each; Part 1 notes are bullet points with short related opinions, and only two bullet points are discussed.
Cambridge 'Checklist to improve your writing: C1 Advanced' (2024): the four Writing criteria Content, Communicative Achievement, Organisation and Language and what each one looks at.
Cambridge 'Teacher guide for writing C1 Advanced': four subscales, each marked 0-5. Seen in search results only; the PDF was too large to open.
C1 Advanced Speaking assessment scales: Grammatical Resource, Lexical Resource, Discourse Management, Pronunciation, Interactive Communication, plus a separate Global Achievement scale; bands 0-5.

writingCriteria.name: Content
writingCriteria.descriptionEn: Whether the answer does everything the task asks: all required points are covered, nothing irrelevant is added, the task is not misread and the points are developed with the writer's own ideas.
writingCriteria.descriptionCs: Zda text splnil vše, co zadání požaduje: pokrývá všechny požadované body, neobsahuje nic nepodstatného, zadání nebylo špatně pochopeno a body jsou rozvedeny vlastními myšlenkami.

writingCriteria.name: Communicative Achievement
writingCriteria.descriptionEn: Whether the text suits the task type and the target reader: it achieves its purpose (for example persuading, recommending, explaining) and uses a suitable register, tone and balance of fact and opinion.
writingCriteria.descriptionCs: Zda text odpovídá typu úlohy a cílovému čtenáři: plní svůj účel (např. přesvědčit, doporučit, vysvětlit) a používá vhodný styl, tón a poměr faktů a názorů.

writingCriteria.name: Organisation
writingCriteria.descriptionEn: How well the text is put together: logical order, clear paragraphs, features that fit the genre (headings, openings, closings) and ideas that are clearly linked and given balanced space.
writingCriteria.descriptionCs: Jak dobře je text uspořádán: logické pořadí, jasné odstavce, prvky odpovídající žánru (nadpisy, oslovení, závěr) a myšlenky zřetelně propojené a vyvážené.

writingCriteria.name: Language
writingCriteria.descriptionEn: The range and accuracy of vocabulary and grammar, including topic-specific phrases and spelling; errors matter most when they make the text hard to follow.
writingCriteria.descriptionCs: Rozsah a přesnost slovní zásoby a gramatiky včetně frází k tématu a pravopisu; nejvíce vadí chyby, které ztěžují porozumění.

speakingCriteria.name: Grammatical Resource
speakingCriteria.descriptionEn: How well the candidate controls a range of grammatical forms, both simple and complex.
speakingCriteria.descriptionCs: Jak dobře kandidát ovládá škálu gramatických struktur, jednoduchých i složitých.

speakingCriteria.name: Lexical Resource
speakingCriteria.descriptionEn: How wide and appropriate the vocabulary is for giving and exchanging views on familiar and less familiar topics.
speakingCriteria.descriptionCs: Jak široká a vhodná je slovní zásoba při vyjadřování a výměně názorů na známá i méně známá témata.

speakingCriteria.name: Discourse Management
speakingCriteria.descriptionEn: Whether the candidate speaks at length with little hesitation, keeps contributions relevant and organised, and links ideas with cohesive devices and discourse markers.
speakingCriteria.descriptionCs: Zda kandidát mluví souvisle a bez větší váhavosti, drží se tématu, má myšlenky uspořádané a propojuje je spojovacími výrazy.

speakingCriteria.name: Pronunciation
speakingCriteria.descriptionEn: How easy the candidate is to understand: intonation, sentence and word stress, and clear individual sounds.
speakingCriteria.descriptionCs: Jak snadno je kandidátovi rozumět: intonace, větný a slovní přízvuk a zřetelná výslovnost jednotlivých hlásek.

speakingCriteria.name: Interactive Communication
speakingCriteria.descriptionEn: How well the candidate starts and responds in the conversation, builds on what the partner says, keeps the discussion moving and works towards an outcome.
speakingCriteria.descriptionCs: Jak dobře kandidát zahajuje a reaguje v rozhovoru, navazuje na partnera, udržuje diskusi v pohybu a směřuje k dohodě.

speakingCriteria.name: Global Achievement
speakingCriteria.descriptionEn: An overall view of the performance: how easily the candidate handles a range of topics, including abstract ones, and produces coherent, accurate extended speech.
speakingCriteria.descriptionCs: Celkový dojem z výkonu: jak snadno kandidát zvládá různá témata včetně abstraktních a jak souvisle a přesně mluví v delších úsecích.

notice.en: This is AI-generated feedback on a practice task. It is not a Cambridge mark, score or grade and does not predict an exam result.
notice.cs: Toto je zpětná vazba vytvořená AI k cvičné úloze. Nejde o hodnocení Cambridge, skóre ani známku a nepředpovídá výsledek zkoušky.

notes: Criterion descriptions are our own paraphrases of public Cambridge materials, not the official band descriptors.

Writing Part 1 input (three bullet points plus three short opinions; discuss two points; opinions optional, in own words) is confirmed by Cambridge teaching resources for the 2015 revised exam (sources 2 and 3). The handbook PDF itself was not opened, so the current handbook wording was not checked.
Writing subscales marked 0-5 each: seen in search results for the teacher guide only (the PDF was too large to open). Not verified this session.
That Global Achievement is given by the interlocutor and the other five criteria by the assessor is not stated in the scale PDF we read. Not verified this session.
Speaking part timings are approximate ('about') on the official page. The app uses them as practice timers only.
The suggested split of about 45 minutes per Writing part is common advice, not an official rule, so it is not included in timings.
